finding: Can checking behavior distinguish source-specific trust from general vigilance? In N15, failures of both the focal and second source improve true-mechanism log loss by 0.009–0.535 nats across twelve settings; focal-source failures alone gain 0.005–0.293 nats and preserve the declared exact alias between source tracking and global vigilance. Added failures become less informative after 32 records. All 12,288 cases, 108 independently reconstructed intervals, six frozen rivals and full replay verify. This is a constructed-mechanism result, not evidence about human trust or attention.
